topic: dependent sibling resampling: stratified priority selection preserves expectation and weakly improves one-step variance

public_evidence.source: Finke, Johansen, Lee, Murray, Resampling in conditional SMC algorithms
public_evidence.result: A general properly-weighted resampling framework covers adaptive and dependent schemes including systematic resampling; validity rests on proper weighting/persistence rather than exchangeability or marginal-unbiasedness folklore.

public_evidence.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering
public_evidence.result: Residual and stratified resampling provably improve on basic multinomial resampling in conditional variance, while systematic resampling has a counterexample and is ordering-sensitive; systematic should not be assumed uniformly lower variance.

public_evidence.source: Li, Wang, Deng, Liu, Stratification and Optimal Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo
public_evidence.result: Stratification/ordered resampling can substantially reduce resampling variance; in one dimension stratified resampling on sorted particles is equivalent to optimal-transport resampling for the stated criteria.

derived_results.claim: Fix a predictable priority proposal q over current parents, base weights W, and M descendants. Partition U in [0,1] into M equal strata, draw U_m independently within stratum m, let A_m=F_q^{-1}(U_m), and generate each descendant truth Y_m under the base continuation law with E[Y_m|A_m=i,past]=p_i. Then T=(1/M)sum_m [W_{A_m}/q_{A_m}]Y_m has conditional expectation sum_i W_i p_i. Independence of ancestor draws is unnecessary; equal-probability stratification plus the importance correction is enough.

Let G(U,Y)=[W_A/q_A]Y with A=F_q^{-1}(U). Multinomial priority sampling has Var(T_iid|past)=Var(G)/M. Stratified sampling has Var(T_strat|past)=M^{-2}sum_m Var(G|U in stratum m). By total variance, Var(G)=E_stratum Var(G|stratum)+Var_stratum E[G|stratum], so Var(T_strat)<=Var(T_iid). The inequality includes both branch-selection and conditional Bernoulli truth noise and holds for any fixed ordering of the q CDF; stratification removes only the between-stratum component and cannot increase the one-step variance.

A single random offset systematic construction also gives the correct ensemble expectation because expected offspring counts equal Mq_i, but shared-offset dependence can create positive covariance across offspring. The Douc-Cappe-Moulines counterexample shows systematic variance can exceed multinomial and depends on particle ordering. A semantic/proxy-sorted agent frontier is therefore exactly the kind of setting where an unexamined periodic ordering can matter.

The particle count may be adaptive without bias if M_t is a positive integer measurable from the past before current offspring are sampled. Conditioning on F_{t-1} and M_t reduces to the fixed-M proof, so compute allocation can respond to prior ESS, prior uncertainty or prior risk evidence. By contrast, stopping descendant generation based on current offspring/labels makes M non-predictable and the naive 1/M normalization is not covered; it needs a proper random-count construction/inclusion weighting rather than an optional-stopping shortcut.

If q=(1-e)q0+eW, then q_i>=eW_i and every child importance ratio W_i/q_i<=1/e exactly as in iid priority sampling. Stratification therefore adds a variance-reduction layer without weakening the support/weight-ratio safety guard or the r118/r119 bounded-loss calculations at the one-step branch-selection level.

design_consequence.claim: For batched independent descendants of a priority-guided agent/search state, use independent stratified uniforms over the explicit defensive priority CDF as the default low-variance resampler instead of iid multinomial. Keep systematic as an optional performance optimization only after ordering-specific testing. Choose descendant count from past state if adaptive compute is needed. Continue to log q and apply separate transition P/Q ratios whenever environment/tool responses are themselves proposal-biased.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The exact variance dominance is a one-step estimator result under independent stratum uniforms and base-conditional descendant truth. Multi-generation SMC variance may have additional interactions even when each resampling step is properly weighted.
Systematic resampling remains valid in suitable proper-weighting frameworks; the negative result concerns a blanket variance-dominance claim, not correctness or usefulness in every ordering.
A predictable random particle count is covered by conditioning; a count chosen using current descendants is not.
If environment/tool transitions are sampled from a proposal rather than the base law, parent resampling weights alone do not identify base deployment risk.
No real-agent or AGI capability conclusion follows.
next_tests: Measure stratified-vs-iid priority variance on multi-generation rare-event trees with common random paths, including semantic/proxy sorting and repeated resampling.
Instantiate Finke proper weighting for a recursive stratified priority SMC state rather than only the one-step estimator, and verify normalizing-constant unbiasedness under the exact index law used.

Test predictable adaptive particle count based on prior paired-CS uncertainty and compare wall-clock/variance efficiency; keep current-generation outcome-dependent stopping out until properly weighted.
Construct an adversarial ordering stress where systematic priority resampling aliases with proxy/risk structure, and quantify whether random permutation or stratified resampling removes the failure.
Combine r119 local material routing with predictable compute allocation: increase M only when the expected value of information exceeds the extra particle cost, without changing estimator target.
